title: Expert Witness Report Excerpt — Landon v. Hightower Industries
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS
224TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-35678-D

MARTHA LANDON, Plaintiff,
v.
HIGHTOWER INDUSTRIES, INC., and JOHN O’NEIL, Individually, Defendants.

EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF DR. ANITA VASQUEZ

I, Dr. Anita Vasquez, being duly sworn, submit this report pursuant to Texas Rule of Evidence 702. My qualifications are attached as Exhibit A (Bates range LAND0001–LAND-0050). I am a board-certified toxicologist with over twenty years of experience, retained by counsel for Plaintiff, Bryant Law Firm (Bar No. 24056789), represented by Deborah Bryant.

1. Summary of Opinions

It is my opinion, to a reasonable degree of scientific certainty, that the Plaintiff, Martha Landon (DOB: 04/12/1978), was exposed to elevated levels of trichloroethylene (TCE) at the Hightower Industries facility located at 1400 Industrial Parkway, Houston, TX 77002. This exposure proximately caused her acute myeloid leukemia, diagnosed in 2023.

2. Factual Background

Martha Landon worked as a maintenance technician at Hightower from June 2005 to August 2022. During deposition, John O’Neil, the former plant manager, stated: "I knew there were leaks in the solvent lines, but [Landon] never complained." The defense expert, Dr. Robert K. Simmons, disagreed with my causation analysis in his report dated 03/15/2024. His phone number is 713-555-0198, and his email is rsimmons@enviriskconsulting.com.

3. Review of Relevant Literature

I have relied upon established epidemiological studies, including a key decision from the Texas Supreme Court: 

Jones v. ChemCorp, Inc., 512 S.W.3d 401 (Tex. 2016). This case established the burden-shifting framework for toxic tort causation. Additionally, a federal decision from the Fifth Circuit, Landry v. Gulf States Utilities, 689 F.3d 412 (5th Cir. 2012), supports the admissibility of differential etiology testimony.

4. Statutory Framework

Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 82.003 governs the liability of successors in products liability actions. Here, Hightower Industries acquired the relevant facility in 2004 from a predecessor, and the statute precludes successor liability unless certain exceptions apply.

5. Specific Findings

A. Exposure Assessment

Plaintiff’s Social Security Number, XXX-XX-8912, was provided for medical records linkage, but I have not used it for any analysis. I reviewed industrial hygiene measurements from the period 2010–2020. The highest TCE concentration was 85 ppm, exceeding the OSHA PEL.

B. Medical Records

Dr. Susan Chen (Plaintiff’s oncologist) provided records including a diagnosis of AML-M4. The patient’s insurance policy number is POL-77234-01, and her vehicle identification number (VIN: 1HGCM82633A004352) appears on an intake form as exhibitJohn Doe attached to deposition Exhibit 3.

C. Defendants’ Alternative Causation Theory

Defendants argue that Plaintiff’s smoking history (40 pack-years) is the sole cause. However, the medical literature does not support smoking as a primary cause of AML.

6. Conclusion

Defense counsel, Williams & Tanaka, represented by Robert Tanaka, has stipulated to my qualifications. The Presiding Judge, Hon. Maria Delgado, entered a scheduling order on 02/01/2024. I reserve the right to supplement this report.

Respectfully submitted,
Dr. Anita Vasquez
Board Certified Toxicologist, No. TX-TOX-4567

VERIFICATION

I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.
Executed on 04/20/2024.

/s/ Anita Vasquez

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I certify that a true copy of this report was served on opposing counsel, Robert Tanaka, at robert.tanaka@williamstanaka.com on 04/21/2024.

[END OF EXCERPT]

title: Expert Witness Report Excerpt — Parkview Medical Center v. Aetna Health Plan
text:
IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF TEXAS
DALLAS DIVISION

CAUSE NO. 3:24-CV-01234-X

PARKVIEW MEDICAL CENTER, Plaintiff,
v.
AETNA HEALTH PLAN OF TEXAS, INC., Defendant.

EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF MARK J. FOSTER, M.D., M.P.H.

I, Mark J. Foster, M.D., M.P.H., submit this report regarding the medical necessity of inpatient hospitalization for Plaintiff’s patient, Mrs. Eleanor Carlisle-James (DOB: 09/22/1965). I am the Chief of Cardiology at Dallas Methodist Hospital (Bar No. TX-12345). My CV is attached as Bates range PKVW-00001–PKVW-00010.

1. Scope of Engagement

Plaintiff Parkview Medical Center retained me to evaluate whether the denial of coverage by Defendant Aetna Health Plan for the period 01/15/2024 through 01/28/2024 was reasonable. The patient’s policy number is AET-998877-01, and her Social Security Number is XXX-XX-4432.

2. Factual Summary

Mrs. Carlisle-James presented to the emergency department with acute coronary syndrome. Dr. Linda O’Hara, the admitting physician, performed an angiogram that revealed 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending artery. In her deposition, Dr. O’Hara testified: "I told [Foster] the patient needed urgent bypass surgery." Aetna’s reviewing physician, Dr. Harold Klein, opined that the admission was not medically necessary, citing internal guidelines.

3. Relevant Authorities

The standard of care for unstable angina is well established. I rely on the Texas Supreme Court’s decision in Gonzalez v. United Healthcare, 601 S.W.3d 210 (Tex. 2020), which held that insurance companies must give deference to treating physicians. Additionally, the Fifth Circuit case Buford v. Blue Cross Blue Shield, 456 F.3d 378 (5th Cir. 2006), defines the scope of ERISA preemption.

4. Statutory Basis

Texas Insurance Code § 1204.151 requires health plans to have an independent review for denials of emergency care. Aetna failed to provide such a review. Defendant’s counsel, the law firm of Klein & Alvarez, represented by attorney Michael Klein, argues that the statute does not apply to self-funded plans.

5. Specific Medical Findings

A. Clinical Course

The patient underwent three-vessel coronary artery bypass grafting on 01/17/2024. Complications included atrial fibrillation. Her length of stay was 13 days. The patient’s phone number, 214-555-0147, and email, eleanor.james@myemail.com, appear on the admission forms.

B. Credentials

I am board certified in internal medicine and cardiology. I have published 15 peer-reviewed articles. My bar number is 24098765. The Presiding Judge in this case is Hon. James Morrison, who issued a protective order on 03/01/2024.

C. Exhibits

Attached as Exhibit M is the patient’s vehicle identification number (VIN: 2FMDK3KC5BBA23456) as listed on the intake form, along with a copy of her driver’s license.

6. Conclusion

It is my opinion, within reasonable medical probability, that the inpatient admission was medically necessary. Aetna’s denial was arbitrary and capricious.

Respectfully submitted,
Mark J. Foster, M.D., M.P.H.

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I served this report on opposing counsel, Michael Klein, at michael.klein@kleinalvarez.com on 04/22/2024.

[END OF EXCERPT]

title: Expert Witness Report Excerpt — Estate of Frank Torres v. City of El Paso
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF EL PASO COUNTY, TEXAS
34TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-CV-00088-E

ESTATE OF FRANK TORRES, DECEASED, BY AND THROUGH ITS ADMINISTRATOR, MARIA TORRES, Plaintiff,
v.
CITY OF EL PASO, TEXAS, Defendant.

EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF SERGEANT DAVID D. RIVERA (RET.)

I, David D. Rivera, former sergeant with the El Paso Police Department (Badge No. 4582), provide this expert report regarding use of force. I am retained by the law firm of O’Malley & Cruz, P.C., Bar No. 24123456, represented by attorney Patrick O’Malley.

1. Qualifications

I served 25 years in law enforcement, including 10 years in the tactical unit. I have testified as an expert in use of force in 30 cases, including State v. Martinez, 450 S.W.3d 345 (Tex. App.—El Paso 2014). I am also familiar with the U.S. Supreme Court case Graham v. Connor, 490 U.S. 386 (1989).

2. Factual Background

On June 17, 2023, Frank Torres (DOB: 03/11/1970) was shot and killed by Officer Kevin Chen after a traffic stop. The City’s internal affairs report (Bates range EPD-001–EPD-045) concluded the shooting was justified. However, the family’s expert, Dr. Linda Green, disagrees. In her report, she noted: "[Rivera] testified that the officer violated policy."

3. Analysis

The use of force continuum, as codified in Tex. Penal Code § 9.51, governs officer conduct. Here, Mr. Torres was unarmed and did not pose an imminent threat. Officer Chen’s phone number, 915-555-0234, and email, kchen@elpasotx.gov, were found in the dispatch logs. Mr. Torres’s Social Security Number was XXX-XX-5678.

4. Evidence Review

A. Video Footage

The dashcam video (Exhibit C) shows the officer shouting commands for 8 seconds before firing. Mr. Torres’s vehicle identification number (VIN: 1N4AL3APXDC123456) is visible on the vehicle registration.

B. Policy Violations

The City’s policy number USE-2022-05 requires de-escalation. Officer Chen did not attempt de-escalation. The City’s attorney, Sarah M. Bryant of Bryant & Associates, argues that the policy does not apply to high-risk stops. The Presiding Judge, Hon. Robert L. Garcia, allowed this expert testimony under Rule 702.

5. Citations and Statutes

I rely on the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals decision in Smith v. State, 478 S.W.3d 231 (Tex. Crim. App. 2015), regarding the reasonableness of deadly force. Additionally, the Fifth Circuit case Thompson v. City of Dallas, 789 F.3d 456 (5th Cir. 2015), is instructive.

6. Conclusion

It is my opinion that Officer Chen used excessive force in violation of department policy and state law. The Estate is entitled to damages.

Respectfully submitted,
David D. Rivera (Ret.)

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I served this report on opposing counsel, Sarah M. Bryant, at sbryant@bryantassociates.com on 04/23/2024.

[END OF EXCERPT]

title: Expert Witness Report Excerpt — Coastal Oil & Gas v. Environmental Protection Commission
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF JEFFERSON COUNTY, TEXAS
58TH JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-02157-B

COASTAL OIL & GAS, LLC, Plaintiff,
v.
TEXAS ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION COMMISSION, Defendant.

EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF CAROLYN H. WELLS, P.E.

I, Carolyn H. Wells, P.E., submit this report regarding groundwater contamination at the Beaumont Refinery site. I am a licensed professional engineer in Texas (License No. 87654). My report is Bates range COG-0001–COG-0030. I am retained by the law firm of Wells & Patterson, but I have no familial relationship with any party.

1. Facts

The Plaintiff, Coastal Oil & Gas, operates a refinery at 2200 Gulf Freeway, Beaumont, TX 77701. The Defendant, Texas Environmental Protection Commission, issued a citation for alleged benzene releases. The plant manager, John C. O’Neil (note: spelling differs from witness in another case), stated: "[Wells] has reviewed our monitoring data."

2. Data Sources

I reviewed groundwater samples from 2019–2023. The Plaintiff’s expert, Dr. Thomas A. Klein of Klein Environmental Services, concluded that contamination originated offsite. His report references the case Exxon v. TCEQ, 345 S.W.3d 234 (Tex. 2011). I also rely on the Fifth Circuit decision, Gulf Coast Refining v. EPA, 567 F.3d 789 (5th Cir. 2009).

3. Statutory Compliance

Tex. Water Code § 26.031 requires permits for discharges. Coastal holds permit No. TX-0078945. The Commission’s lead attorney, Deborah Bryant of Bryant Law Firm, argues that the permit does not cover fugitive emissions. The Presiding Judge, Hon. Katherine A. Nguyen, set trial for October 2024.

4. Specifics

A. Site Inspection

On 02/15/2024, I observed a leaking pipe. The Social Security Number of a nearby resident, Mrs. Gladys Patterson (DOB: 11/30/1950), was inadvertently included in the site log: XXX-XX-3345. Her phone is 409-555-0199, and her email is gpatterson@myemail.com.

B. Equipment

The VIN of the sampling truck is 3C6UR5JL7JG123456. The Commission’s policy number for enforcement is ENF-2022-08.

C. Exhibits

Attached as exhibitJohn Smith is a photograph of the pipe leak. Mr. Smith is a former employee.

5. Conclusion

I conclude that the Commission’s citation is not supported by the evidence. The benzene levels are within regulatory limits.

Respectfully submitted,
Carolyn H. Wells, P.E.

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I served this report on opposing counsel, Deborah Bryant, at dbryant@bryantlawfirm.com on 04/24/2024.

[END OF EXCERPT]

title: Expert Witness Report Excerpt — In re Adoption of Minor Child Jackson
text:
IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS
201ST JUDICIAL DISTRICT

CAUSE NO. 2024-ADOPT-00054

IN THE INTEREST OF JACKSON, A MINOR CHILD

EXPERT WITNESS REPORT OF DR. KAREN O’NEAL-MARTINEZ

I, Dr. Karen O’Neal-Martinez, Psy.D., submit this report in connection with the adoption of the minor child, Jackson (DOB: 06/14/2019). I am a licensed psychologist in Texas (License No. 34567). My report is Bates range JAX-100–JAX-115. I was retained by the law firm of Carter & Associates, represented by attorney Thomas Carter.

1. Evaluation Summary

I conducted a psychological evaluation of the biological mother, Cynthia O’Neil (note: hyphenated surname not used here), and the prospective adoptive parents, Mr. and Mrs. Harrison Bryant III. The child’s Social Security Number is XXX-XX-9012. The biological father is unknown. The Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (DFPS) is a party. DFPS’s attorney is Sarah Klein, of Klein & Alvarez.

2. Recommendations

I recommend termination of parental rights of Cynthia O’Neil and placement with the Bryants. In my interview, Ms. O’Neil stated: "I want [O’Neal-Martinez] to tell the judge I’m fit." However, her history of substance abuse contradicts this. The child’s phone number (512-555-0187) and email (temporary@state.tx.us) are on file.

3. Legal Framework

The Texas Family Code § 161.001 governs termination grounds. I rely on the Texas Supreme Court case In re K.Y., 567 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. 2019), which emphasizes the best interest of the child. Also relevant is the Fifth Circuit case L.F. v. Houston ISD, 789 F.3d 123 (5th Cir. 2015), regarding educational rights.

4. Observations

A. Psychological Testing

Ms. O’Neil scored in the clinical range on the MMPI-3. The VIN of the Bryant family car is 5YJSA1E26KF123456, provided in their home study.

B. Policy Compliance

DFPS policy number ADOPT-2021-04 requires home visits. The home study was completed. The Presiding Judge, Hon. Patricia O’Brien, ordered an expedited hearing.

5. Conclusion

Termination and adoption are in the child’s best interest.

Respectfully submitted,
Dr. Karen O’Neal-Martinez

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

I served this report on opposing counsel, Sarah Klein, at sklein@kleinalvarez.com on 04/25/2024.

[END OF EXCERPT]
